name: Knock Rummy
description: Knock Rummy is a fast-paced variant of the classic Rummy family. Unlike standard Rummy where players must wait for a 'Gin' or empty their hand, in Knock Rummy any player can end the round by 'knocking' after their discard, provided they believe their unmatched card points (deadwood) are lower than their opponents'. It is a game of risk-assessment and speed.

history.origins: Developed in the early 20th century as a quicker alternative to the lengthy '500 Rummy' matches. It directly influenced the development of Gin Rummy.
timeline: 1910s: Knock Rummy first documented in American card manuals.
1930s: Gin Rummy surpasses it in popularity due to its more complex 'bonus' structure.
Present: Remains a popular family game, especially in the US and Canada.
history.cultural: Commonly played as a betting game where each point in the deadwood count has a set monetary value.
history.evolution: The 'Knock' mechanic introduced a new strategic dimensionâ€”forcing the end of a round before an opponent can complete their sets.

setup.players: 2 players (10 cards each), 3-5 players (7 cards each).
setup.deck: Standard 52-card deck. Aces are low (1) or high (11) depending on house rules.
setup.dealing: Cards are dealt face-down; one card is turned up to start the discard pile.

rules.objective: Form sets (3-4 of a kind) and runs (3+ in suit) and have the lowest point total of unmatched cards (deadwood) when the round ends.
rules.gameplay:
1. Draw one card from the stock or discard pile.
2. Form melds in hand (but do not lay them down on the table until the end).
3. End of Turn: Discard one card. If you wish to end the round, announce 'Knock' before or during the discard.
keyRules: Form sets (3-4 of a kind) and runs (3+ consecutive in suit)
Draw from stock or discard pile
Can knock at any point after draw
No laying off on opponent's melds

strategy.basic: Knock early. If you have two sets and your remaining 3 cards are an Ace-2-3, you have very low points (6). Knocking early prevents your opponent from finishing their high-value runs.
strategy.intermediate: The 'High Card Dump': If you aren't close to a meld, discard your Kings and Queens first. Your goal is to keep your deadwood total low in case someone else knocks suddenly.
strategy.advanced: Baiting the Discard: Discard a card that you think your opponent doesn't need, even if it fits your hypothetical run, to keep the stock pile moving without giving them an advantage.
tips: If you draw from the discard pile, you are signaling what rank you are collecting. Use the stock pile instead if you want to keep your strategy secret.
Don't knock if you have more than 20 points in deadwoodâ€”the risk of being 'under-cut' is too high.

scoring.description: Winner has lowest deadwood. Scores difference from opponents. Gin bonus (25 pts) for zero deadwood. Under-cut bonus (10 pts) if lower than knocker.

synthesis.shortDescription: Knock Rummy is a Rummy variant where players can end the round by knocking when they believe their deadwood is lowest.
